note: The fictional Atlas service pavilion on the real gravel plateau ~50 m east of the Rotunda (DECISIONS item 6), painted as its exterior with the open service bay (orchestrator brief: S48 exterior, S49 interior). Camera ~1.7 m high on the plateau, looking west at the Rotunda complex as in the 2016 photos taken from the summit path; horizon y ~470; the Rotunda's entrance and its external steel stairs stand far back on y ~560, the pavilion's front on the right stands on y ~765 (~160 px per metre there). Perspective s(y) = (y - 470) / 545. Left/centre: the Rotunda (stone base, red band with the lettering ROTUNDA CHOPOK, glass drum, red ring roof) between the dark station wings, the steel stairs up to the roof terrace; the gravel plateau with rocks, dwarf pine and June snow patches; right: the modular timber-and-white pavilion of the exhibition with its open service bay (terminal on a rugged cart, a taped paper note beside it, cables on the gravel) and the door to the inner chamber. The walk polygon follows the open gravel path only: the dwarf pine, the rocks and the snow patches of the painting on both sides of the path stay outside it; in front of the pavilion door it is a narrow strip.
